CHAPTER 39  Medical Nutrition Therapy for Rheumatic Disease
A physical examination provides diagnostic signs and symp-
toms of nutrient deficiencies (see Appendix 29). Current weight 
and history of weight change over time are the least expensive, 
least invasive, and most reliable assessment tools to use. Weight 
change is an important measure of RA severity. The character-
istic progression of malnutrition in RA is attributed to excessive 
protein catabolism evoked by inflammatory cytokines and by 
disuse atrophy resulting from functional impairment.
The diet history should review the usual diet; the effect of 
the handicap; types of food consumed; and changes in food 
tolerance secondary to oral, esophageal, and intestinal disor-
ders. The effect of the disease on food shopping and prepara-
tion, self-feeding ability, appetite, and intake also must be as-
sessed. The use of elimination or other diets purported to treat 
or cure arthritis should be identified.
